verdict.rationale: PostHog's self-host docs say the product is open-source and free for anyone to host themselves, with a free Docker Compose deployment under an MIT license. That clearly delivers the core of the story. A community report of a broken production Dockerfile dates from the product's early launch thread and is a dated, one-off bug, not a contradiction of the current documented deployment, so it lowers confidence only. Missing for 10: detail on which features and scale the self-hosted deployment supports versus cloud, setup and operations documentation depth, and recent independent hands-on corroboration that self-hosting works.
